patch_description:
Key ideas:
- Encode tic-tac-toe winning structure explicitly by adding CCRZ interactions on every winning line (shared parameter "ccrz_line") so the circuit can directly sense three-in-a-row correlations.
- Use Multi-Z (ZZZ) rotations separated into row/column vs diagonal groups ("zzz_rowcol", "zzz_diag") to capture collective parity along those geometries.
- Maintain light-weight, symmetry-aware single-qubit rotations (shared corner/edge/center RY and RZ) for parameter efficiency and to respect board symmetries.
- Add a single shared RX mixing rotation ("rx_shared") on every qubit to increase expressivity without exploding parameter count.
- Keep parametrized controlled-Z couplings around the outer ring ("crz_ring") and radial couplings to center ("crz_to_center"), plus controlled-X radial couplings ("crx_to_center") to give both phase and amplitude entangling channels.

Why this should improve performance:
- Directly providing CCRZ and ZZZ motifs on the eight winning lines gives the optimizer the ability to form features aligned with the task's combinatorial structure (detecting 3-in-a-row), improving sample efficiency and classification accuracy.
- Symmetry-based parameter sharing reduces overfitting and the train-test gap while keeping expressive nonlocal interactions available (via CCRZ/ZZZ).
- Mixing both CRZ and CRX radial couplings gives complementary entangling mechanisms for center-vs-edge signals (important because center participates in many winning lines).
- Overall parameter budget per block remains compact (13 keys), keeping total N_PARAMS similar to prior designs but shifting expressivity into structured multi-qubit motifs that directly match the problem geometry.
